CreateReimbursementFromReceiptRequestBod.description:
Create a reimbursement from an actual uploaded receipt. The receipt is identified by
its real UUID from the conversation context or receipt-matching handoff.

Do not use this tool for mileage reimbursements. Do not call this tool unless a real
receipt UUID is available. Never pass placeholders such as null, "null", "mileage",
or 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000.

When you have extracted receipt details from the image, provide amount, currency_code,
transaction_date, and merchant directly. This creates the draft faster and more reliably
than OCR. At minimum, provide the amount. Omit fields you could not extract.

After successfully creating the reimbursement:
1. Check missing_items to see what is required
2. For items that CAN be filled via the agent (memo, accounting categories, funds, trip, attendees):
   - Request the missing item from the user
   - Include the relevant suggestions (suggested_memos or suggested_codings)
   - For funds, consult suggested_funds alongside the user's expense history and any
     preference the user has stated. suggested_funds is ordered by policy preference
     (most preferred first). Submitting without a fund appears as a
     regular entry (fund_name="None", fund_uuid="00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000")
     when policy permits it — treat it like any other choice and refer to it as "None"
     to the user.
3. For items that CANNOT be filled via the agent (mileage_locations, or if all agent-fillable items are complete):
   - ALWAYS provide the reimbursement_link URL as a clickable link in your response
   - Format it as markdown: [link text](reimbursement_link)
   - Example: "You can complete your reimbursement here: [Complete reimbursement](https://app.ramp.com:3000/s/reimbursements/xxx)"

Items are requested in this order: receipt, memo, accounting categories, funds.

EditTransactionRequestBody.description:
Edit a transaction field. The supported edit types are memo, funds, accounting category, trip, and attendees.
This tool allows updating specific fields of a transaction that the user has
permission to edit. Provide at least one field to update.

After successfully editing the transaction:
1. Check missing_items to see what is required
2. For items that CAN be filled via the agent (memo, accounting categories, funds, trip, attendees):
   - Request the missing item from the user
   - Include the relevant suggestions (suggested_memos, suggested_codings, or suggested_funds)
3. For items that CANNOT be filled via the agent (if all agent-fillable items are complete):
   - ALWAYS provide the transaction_link URL as a clickable link in your response
   - Format it as markdown: [link text](transaction_link)
   - Example: "You can complete your transaction here: [Complete transaction](https://app.ramp.com/transactions/xxx)"

Items are requested in this order: receipt, memo, accounting categories, funds, trip, attendees.

If there are no missing items left, the agent should confirm with the user if they want to submit the transaction.

- What they can buy from a specific fund

LimitIncreaseRequestBody.description:
Increase the spending limit on a fund (spend allocation) or card.

REQUIRED MULTI-STEP PROTOCOL — do NOT call this tool until both conditions are met:
1. The user has clearly stated whether the increase should be TEMPORARY or PERMANENT.
   - If they haven't specified, ask: "Would you like this to be a temporary increase
     (resets at the end of the current period) or a permanent increase?"
   - Do NOT guess or default to either option.
2. Once the user confirms, set increase_type to "temporary" or "permanent" AND
   set user_confirmed_increase_type to True.

A temporary increase resets at the next interval boundary (e.g., end of month).
A permanent increase persists indefinitely.
If the user does not specify a fund or card, ask them to specify one.

Use this when a user wants to:
- Temporarily increase their fund limit for the current period (e.g., "I need more budget this month")
- Permanently increase their fund or card limit
- Increase their card limit (e.g., "increase my card ending in 1234 to $200")
- Request a higher spending limit

card_id.title: Card Id

SearchFlightOffersRequestBody.description:
Search for flight offers using AI-powered recommendations.

TEMPORARY GUARDRAIL: Do NOT use this tool to help the user change, modify, cancel,
rebook, swap, or replace an existing booking. For existing booking changes, direct the
user to the Ramp web app instead of searching replacement flights through the agent.

Do NOT use this tool until the minimum search intake checklist below is satisfied.
Once the user has provided the required itinerary details, use this tool immediately instead of
asking extra exploratory questions. The tool reads travel preferences internally, so you do not
need to call GetTravelPreferences in advance. Only fall back to GetFlightBookingLocations if this
tool cannot run because the origin or destination needs additional disambiguation.

MINIMUM SEARCH INTAKE BEFORE CALLING THIS TOOL:
If the user has not already provided the itinerary, collect the missing search-critical fields in
one friendly sentence instead of a vague follow-up question or rigid form. Confirm these fields
before calling the tool:
 1. destination
 2. departure date
 3. trip type (one-way or round-trip)
 4. return date, if round-trip
 5. departure city or airport, unless the traveler's profile location clearly applies

If the user says something vague like "book a flight" or references an earlier option,
screenshot, or prior search without enough active itinerary context, do NOT call this tool yet.
Ask for the missing essentials in one message, for example: "For sure - I can search once I
have your origin, dates, and whether this is one-way or roundtrip."

If the destination name itself is ambiguous (for example, Portland could mean Oregon or Maine),
clarify which city or airport the user means before searching. If other required fields are also
missing, combine that clarification with the rest of the intake in one natural message.

If the user gives ambiguous airport or city options, keep the clarification friendly and specific.
For example: "Do you want me to search LGB, SNA, or both?"

This tool returns at most 3 intelligently filtered flight offers per call based on
the user's booking history and preferences. The AI analyzes past bookings to recommend
appropriate filters (e.g., non-stop flights, specific airlines, time preferences).

SHOWING MORE OPTIONS: If the user asks for more options, call this tool again with
the same search parameters and set `offset` to the number of results already shown
(e.g., offset=3 after the first batch, offset=6 after the second).

ROUNDTRIP STEP-BY-STEP FLOW (CRITICAL):
For roundtrip flights (when end_date is provided), this tool uses a mandatory two-step search.
You MUST complete BOTH steps before offering to book:
 1. Step 1 — outbound (no selected_outbound_offer_id): Returns outbound flights only.
     search_step='outbound', return_flights=null.
     Present ONLY the outbound options and ask the user to pick one. Do NOT offer to book yet.
     Use the same summary format as one-way results: departure airport code, flight,
     duration, stops, price.
     PRICES ARE ROUND-TRIP: All prices shown in step 1 are full ROUND-TRIP prices (not one-way).
     If the user asks, confirm these are round-trip prices. Do NOT call them "one-way" prices.
  2. Step 2 — return (with selected_outbound_offer_id): Call this tool AGAIN with
     selected_outbound_offer_id set to the user's chosen flight id. Returns return flights only.
     search_step='return', return_flights populated.
     Present the return options and ask the user to pick one. THEN offer to book using
     the selected return flight's id (it contains both legs — see BookFlight for details).
     Use the same summary format here too: departure airport code, flight, duration,
     stops, price.
     PRICES ARE ROUND-TRIP: Step 2 prices are also full round-trip prices for each
     outbound+return combination. Use the selected return flight's price as the final
     round-trip total when confirming with the user.
   If used_out_of_policy_fallback was true in step 1, pass step1_used_out_of_policy_fallback=true.
   If suggested_step2_filters is present in step 1 results, pass it as the `filters` parameter
   in step 2 to ensure consistent cabin class across both legs.

For one-way flights, just omit end_date — no step-by-step needed. Use the same summary
format: departure airport code, flight, duration, stops, price.

CARRY-ON DEFAULT: By default, only fares with carry-on bag included are shown.
If the user wants to see all fares (including basic economy without carry-on),
set filters={"carryon_included": false}.

FILTER OVERRIDES: If the user explicitly requests specific filters, provide a `filters` object.
User-specified filters override AI recommendations. If a filter is restricted by travel policy,
the tool will explain why.

Example filter requests from users:
- "Find me Delta or United flights" -> filters={"airlines": ["DL", "UA"]}
- "I need a direct flight" -> filters={"max_stops": 0}
- "Premium economy please" -> filters={"cabin_class": "PREMIUM_ECONOMY"}
- "Morning flights only" -> filters={"departure_time_after": "06:00", "departure_time_before": "12:00"}
- "Under $500" -> filters={"max_price": 500}
- "Show me all fares including basic economy" -> filters={"carryon_included": false}

FARE OPTIONS: Each flight may include `fare_options` — alternative fare classes for the
same itinerary (e.g., Basic Economy, Main Cabin, First Class). However, do NOT show
fare upgrade options by default. Only present fare options when the user explicitly asks
about upgrades, different fare classes, or cabin class options. When the user does ask:
1. Present the default fare (top-level fields) along with available fare options
2. Show key differences: price, included amenities (bags, seat selection, changes, refunds)
3. Highlight which options are in-policy vs out-of-policy
4. To book a specific fare option, pass its `id` to BookFlight (not the top-level flight `id`)

PRESENTING RESULTS: When showing flight options to users:
1. If `suggested_fund` is present, recommend it using the exact sentence:
   "Recommend booking on *[suggested_fund.fund_name]* funds."
2. If `suggested_fund` is null, tell the user that no existing travel funds were found
   and that booking will request new funds for them. Example: "I couldn't find an
   existing travel fund on your account, so booking will create a new one for you."
3. If `requires_approval` is True, mention the booking may need manager approval
4. Let users change the suggested fund if they prefer a different one
5. Do NOT proactively show fare upgrade options — only show the default in-policy fare
   for each flight. If the user asks about upgrades or other fare classes, then present
   the fare_options so they can compare
6. Always include the departure airport code for each option, and order the
   summary line as airport code, flight, duration, stops, price
   (e.g., "SFO • Delta DL0405 • 5h 29m • Nonstop • $299"). This applies to
   one-way searches and both steps of roundtrip searches.
7. Use the EXACT text from amenity fields (carryon_bag_info, seat_selection_info, etc.)
   — do NOT rephrase. For example, say "Seat selection included" not "Advance seat selection"
8. Do NOT say "Here are your flight options from [Fund Name]."
9. If a flight option includes `departure_date` or `arrival_date`, use those exact
   strings when showing dates. Do NOT infer or recompute the weekday from the numeric date.

Example response format (with fund):
"Recommend booking on *[suggested_fund.fund_name]* funds.
Upgrades may be available, subject to approval. Want to explore them,
or reply 1 or 2 to choose your flight."

Example response format (no fund found):
"Here are your flight options. I didn't find an existing travel fund, so booking
will request new funds for you. Reply 1 or 2 to choose your flight."

BOOKING ON BEHALF OF OTHERS:
If the user is a delegate or travel manager and wants to book for someone else,
pass the traveler's user_id as `traveler_user_id`. The search will use the
traveler's preferences and profile. The same `traveler_user_id` must be passed
to BookFlight when booking.

IMPORTANT — @MENTIONS ARE NOT DELEGATE BOOKINGS:
If the user merely mentions another person in the message without explicitly asking
to search or book *for* or *on behalf of* that person, do NOT set `traveler_user_id`.
A mention alone does not indicate delegate booking intent. Only set `traveler_user_id`
when the user clearly states they want to search or book travel for someone else.

post.description:
TEMPORARY GUARDRAIL: Do NOT use this tool to help the user change, modify, cancel,
rebook, swap, or replace an existing booking. For existing booking changes, direct the
user to the Ramp web app instead of searching replacement flights through the agent.

Do NOT use this tool until the minimum search intake checklist below is satisfied.
Once the user has provided the required itinerary details, use this tool immediately instead of
asking extra exploratory questions. The tool reads travel preferences internally, so you do not
need to call GetTravelPreferences in advance. Only fall back to GetFlightBookingLocations if this
tool cannot run because the origin or destination needs additional disambiguation.

MINIMUM SEARCH INTAKE BEFORE CALLING THIS TOOL:
If the user has not already provided the itinerary, collect the missing search-critical fields in
one friendly sentence instead of a vague follow-up question or rigid form. Confirm these fields
before calling the tool:
 1. destination
 2. departure date
 3. trip type (one-way or round-trip)
 4. return date, if round-trip
 5. departure city or airport, unless the traveler's profile location clearly applies

If the user says something vague like "book a flight" or references an earlier option,
screenshot, or prior search without enough active itinerary context, do NOT call this tool yet.
Ask for the missing essentials in one message, for example: "For sure - I can search once I
have your origin, dates, and whether this is one-way or roundtrip."

If the destination name itself is ambiguous (for example, Portland could mean Oregon or Maine),
clarify which city or airport the user means before searching. If other required fields are also
missing, combine that clarification with the rest of the intake in one natural message.

If the user gives ambiguous airport or city options, keep the clarification friendly and specific.
For example: "Do you want me to search LGB, SNA, or both?"

This tool returns at most 3 intelligently filtered flight offers per call based on
the user's booking history and preferences. The AI analyzes past bookings to recommend
appropriate filters (e.g., non-stop flights, specific airlines, time preferences).

SHOWING MORE OPTIONS: If the user asks for more options, call this tool again with
the same search parameters and set `offset` to the number of results already shown
(e.g., offset=3 after the first batch, offset=6 after the second).

ROUNDTRIP STEP-BY-STEP FLOW (CRITICAL):
For roundtrip flights (when end_date is provided), this tool uses a mandatory two-step search.
You MUST complete BOTH steps before offering to book:
 1. Step 1 — outbound (no selected_outbound_offer_id): Returns outbound flights only.
     search_step='outbound', return_flights=null.
     Present ONLY the outbound options and ask the user to pick one. Do NOT offer to book yet.
     Use the same summary format as one-way results: departure airport code, flight,
     duration, stops, price.
     PRICES ARE ROUND-TRIP: All prices shown in step 1 are full ROUND-TRIP prices (not one-way).
     If the user asks, confirm these are round-trip prices. Do NOT call them "one-way" prices.
  2. Step 2 — return (with selected_outbound_offer_id): Call this tool AGAIN with
     selected_outbound_offer_id set to the user's chosen flight id. Returns return flights only.
     search_step='return', return_flights populated.
     Present the return options and ask the user to pick one. THEN offer to book using
     the selected return flight's id (it contains both legs — see BookFlight for details).
     Use the same summary format here too: departure airport code, flight, duration,
     stops, price.
     PRICES ARE ROUND-TRIP: Step 2 prices are also full round-trip prices for each
     outbound+return combination. Use the selected return flight's price as the final
     round-trip total when confirming with the user.
   If used_out_of_policy_fallback was true in step 1, pass step1_used_out_of_policy_fallback=true.
   If suggested_step2_filters is present in step 1 results, pass it as the `filters` parameter
   in step 2 to ensure consistent cabin class across both legs.

For one-way flights, just omit end_date — no step-by-step needed. Use the same summary
format: departure airport code, flight, duration, stops, price.

CARRY-ON DEFAULT: By default, only fares with carry-on bag included are shown.
If the user wants to see all fares (including basic economy without carry-on),
set filters={"carryon_included": false}.

FILTER OVERRIDES: If the user explicitly requests specific filters, provide a `filters` object.
User-specified filters override AI recommendations. If a filter is restricted by travel policy,
the tool will explain why.

Example filter requests from users:
- "Find me Delta or United flights" -> filters={"airlines": ["DL", "UA"]}
- "I need a direct flight" -> filters={"max_stops": 0}
- "Premium economy please" -> filters={"cabin_class": "PREMIUM_ECONOMY"}
- "Morning flights only" -> filters={"departure_time_after": "06:00", "departure_time_before": "12:00"}
- "Under $500" -> filters={"max_price": 500}
- "Show me all fares including basic economy" -> filters={"carryon_included": false}

FARE OPTIONS: Each flight may include `fare_options` — alternative fare classes for the
same itinerary (e.g., Basic Economy, Main Cabin, First Class). However, do NOT show
fare upgrade options by default. Only present fare options when the user explicitly asks
about upgrades, different fare classes, or cabin class options. When the user does ask:
1. Present the default fare (top-level fields) along with available fare options
2. Show key differences: price, included amenities (bags, seat selection, changes, refunds)
3. Highlight which options are in-policy vs out-of-policy
4. To book a specific fare option, pass its `id` to BookFlight (not the top-level flight `id`)

PRESENTING RESULTS: When showing flight options to users:
1. If `suggested_fund` is present, recommend it using the exact sentence:
   "Recommend booking on *[suggested_fund.fund_name]* funds."
2. If `suggested_fund` is null, tell the user that no existing travel funds were found
   and that booking will request new funds for them. Example: "I couldn't find an
   existing travel fund on your account, so booking will create a new one for you."
3. If `requires_approval` is True, mention the booking may need manager approval
4. Let users change the suggested fund if they prefer a different one
5. Do NOT proactively show fare upgrade options — only show the default in-policy fare
   for each flight. If the user asks about upgrades or other fare classes, then present
   the fare_options so they can compare
6. Always include the departure airport code for each option, and order the
   summary line as airport code, flight, duration, stops, price
   (e.g., "SFO • Delta DL0405 • 5h 29m • Nonstop • $299"). This applies to
   one-way searches and both steps of roundtrip searches.
7. Use the EXACT text from amenity fields (carryon_bag_info, seat_selection_info, etc.)
   — do NOT rephrase. For example, say "Seat selection included" not "Advance seat selection"
8. Do NOT say "Here are your flight options from [Fund Name]."
9. If a flight option includes `departure_date` or `arrival_date`, use those exact
   strings when showing dates. Do NOT infer or recompute the weekday from the numeric date.

Example response format (with fund):
"Recommend booking on *[suggested_fund.fund_name]* funds.
Upgrades may be available, subject to approval. Want to explore them,
or reply 1 or 2 to choose your flight."

Example response format (no fund found):
"Here are your flight options. I didn't find an existing travel fund, so booking
will request new funds for you. Reply 1 or 2 to choose your flight."

BOOKING ON BEHALF OF OTHERS:
If the user is a delegate or travel manager and wants to book for someone else,
pass the traveler's user_id as `traveler_user_id`. The search will use the
traveler's preferences and profile. The same `traveler_user_id` must be passed
to BookFlight when booking.

IMPORTANT — @MENTIONS ARE NOT DELEGATE BOOKINGS:
If the user merely mentions another person in the message without explicitly asking
to search or book *for* or *on behalf of* that person, do NOT set `traveler_user_id`.
A mention alone does not indicate delegate booking intent. Only set `traveler_user_id`
when the user clearly states they want to search or book travel for someone else.
